source.text: הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה בִּשְׁלֹ֨חַ אֵלָ֜יו הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ אֶת־פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן־מַלְכִּיָּ֔ה וְאֶת־צְפַנְיָ֧ה בֶן־מַעֲשֵׂיָ֛ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: The word which came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh, when sent to him the king Zedekiah Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying:

en.L: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying:
en.B: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the time King Zedekiah sent Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah the priest, son of Maaseiah, to him with this request:
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah. It came when King Zedekiah sent two men to him, Pashhur son of Malchiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They said to Jeremiah:

es.L: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, cuando el rey Sedequías le envió a Pasur hijo de Malquías y a Sofonías hijo de Maasías, el sacerdote, diciendo:
es.B: Este mensaje vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} cuando el rey Sedequías le envió a Pasur hijo de Malquías y al sacerdote Sofonías hijo de Maasías con esta petición:
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Jeremías. Llegó cuando el rey Sedequías le envió a dos hombres, Pasur hijo de Malquías y el sacerdote Sofonías hijo de Maasías. Ellos le dijeron a Jeremías:

fr.L: La parole qui fut adressée à Jérémie de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, quand le roi Sédécias lui envoya Pashhour fils de Malkiya et Sophonie fils de Maaséya, le prêtre, pour dire :
fr.B: Ce message fut adressé à Jérémie par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au moment où le roi Sédécias lui envoya Pashhour fils de Malkiya et le prêtre Sophonie fils de Maaséya, avec cette demande :
fr.R: Voici le message que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné à Jérémie. C’était au moment où le roi Sédécias lui a envoyé deux hommes, Pashhour, fils de Malkiya, et le prêtre Sophonie, fils de Maaséya. Ils ont dit à Jérémie :

sw.L: Neno lililomjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, mfalme Sedekia alipomtumia Pashuri mwana wa Malkiya, na Sefania mwana wa Maaseya kuhani, kusema:
sw.B: Ujumbe huu ulimjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakati Mfalme Sedekia alipomtumia Pashuri mwana wa Malkiya na Sefania kuhani, mwana wa Maaseya, wakiwa na ombi hili:
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Yeremia. Ulikuja wakati Mfalme Sedekia alipowatuma watu wawili kwake, Pashuri mwana wa Malkiya na kuhani Sefania mwana wa Maaseya. Wakamwambia Yeremia:

vi.L: Lời từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Giê-rê-mi, khi vua Sê-đê-kia sai Pha-su-rơ con trai Manh-ki-gia và thầy tế lễ Sô-phô-ni con trai Ma-a-sê-gia đến với ông, nói rằng:
vi.B: Sứ điệp này từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Giê-rê-mi vào lúc vua Sê-đê-kia sai Pha-su-rơ con trai Manh-ki-gia và thầy tế lễ Sô-phô-ni con trai Ma-a-sê-gia đến xin ông:
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho Giê-rê-mi. Sứ điệp đến khi vua Sê-đê-kia sai hai người đến gặp ông, là Pha-su-rơ con trai Manh-ki-gia và thầy tế lễ Sô-phô-ni con trai Ma-a-sê-gia. Họ nói với Giê-rê-mi:

ko.L: 시드기야 왕이 말기야의 아들 바스훌과 마아세야의 아들 제사장 스바냐를 예레미야에게 보내어 말하게 했을 때, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 예레미야에게 임한 말씀이다.
ko.B: 이것은 시드기야 왕이 말기야의 아들 바스훌과 마아세야의 아들 제사장 스바냐를 예레미야에게 보내어 부탁했을 때, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 예레미야에게 주신 말씀이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 예레미야에게 주신 말씀은 이러하다. 그 말씀은 시드기야 왕이 두 사람을 예레미야에게 보냈을 때에 임했다. 그 두 사람은 말기야의 아들 바스훌과 마아세야의 아들 제사장 스바냐였다. 그들이 예레미야에게 말했다.

pt.L: A palavra que veio a Jeremias da parte {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, quando o rei Zedequias enviou a ele Pasur, filho de Malquias, e Sofonias, filho de Maaseias, o sacerdote, dizendo:
pt.B: Esta mensagem veio a Jeremias da parte {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} quando o rei Zedequias lhe enviou Pasur, filho de Malquias, e o sacerdote Sofonias, filho de Maaseias, com este pedido:
pt.R: Esta é a mensagem que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu a Jeremias. Ela veio quando o rei Zedequias mandou dois homens até ele: Pasur, filho de Malquias, e o sacerdote Sofonias, filho de Maaseias. Eles disseram a Jeremias:

decisions.choice: Pashhur son of Malchiah: a royal official, not the Pashhur son of Immer of 20:1-6
decisions.reason: The name was common. The Pashhur of chapter 20 was a priest, the son of Immer, who had Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks. This Pashhur is the son of Malchiah, a member of the king's court; he is named again in 38:1 among the officials who wanted Jeremiah put to death. The two men are not the same person, even though the chapters stand side by side.

decisions.choice: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah is the priest
decisions.reason: "The priest" belongs to Zephaniah. He appears again as a priest in charge in the temple (29:25-29), as one of the king's messengers to Jeremiah (37:3), and as "the second priest" taken by the Babylonians when the city fell (52:24; 2 Kings 25:18).

decisions.choice: the setting: the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem under Zedekiah (about 588 BC)
decisions.reason: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah, set on the throne by Nebuchadrezzar (2 Kings 24:17). When he rebelled, the Babylonian army came and besieged Jerusalem (39:1; 52:4). The book is not arranged in time order: this chapter comes some twenty years after the temple sermon of chapter 7. A similar request from Zedekiah is told in 37:3-10.

decisions.choice: the heading names the occasion; the LORD's answer begins in verse 4
decisions.reason: "The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD" introduces the whole chapter. The king's request follows in verse 2, Jeremiah's reply in verse 3, and the word of the LORD itself from verse 4.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah. Balanced says "with this request" for "saying", and Readable breaks the long sentence and names the two men as messengers.

decisions.choice: Pasur hijo de Malquías, Sofonías hijo de Maasías
decisions.reason: The names follow the published Spanish forms (Pasur, Malquías, Sofonías, Maasías). This Pasur is a royal official, not the priest of 20:1 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Pashuri mwana wa Malkiya
decisions.reason: Malchiah takes the form "Malkiya" of 1 Chronicles 24:9; this Pashuri is not the son of Imeri of 20:1, as meaning decision m1 says.

decisions.choice: "Pashhour fils de Malkiya", "Sophonie fils de Maaséya"
decisions.reason: The French forms used for these names in Jeremiah 18-34; Zephaniah takes the usual French "Sophonie", the name of the prophet's book. Pashhour keeps the spelling of 20:1, though this is another man (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "Pha-su-rơ con trai Manh-ki-gia"; "Sô-phô-ni con trai Ma-a-sê-gia"
decisions.reason: The published forms of these names (1 Chronicles 6:21; 9:12; 15:18). This Pashhur is a different man from the priest of 20:1, as meaning decision m1 says; the father's name tells them apart.

decisions.choice: "말기야의 아들 바스훌"; "마아세야의 아들 제사장 스바냐"
decisions.reason: Published Korean forms (말기야, 바스훌 as 1 Chronicles 9:12; 마아세야; 스바냐). This Pashhur is a royal official, not the priest of 20:1 (meaning decision m1); the father's name keeps them apart.

decisions.choice: Pasur, filho de Malquias; Sofonias, filho de Maaseias
decisions.reason: The names take their usual Brazilian forms: "Pasur", the same form as the priest of chapter 20, though this is another man (m1), and "Sofonias", the form 2 Kings 25:18 gives this priest in Portuguese (m2); "Malquias" and "Maaseias" end in "-ias" like the other names in -yah.

source.text: דְּרָשׁ־נָ֤א בַעֲדֵ֨נוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל נִלְחָ֣ם עָלֵ֑ינוּ אוּלַי֩ יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה אוֹתָ֨נוּ֙ כְּכָל־נִפְלְאֹתָ֔יו וְיַעֲלֶ֖ה מֵעָלֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Seek please on behalf of us Yahweh, for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon [is] making war against us; perhaps will do Yahweh with us according to all his wonders, and he will go up from on us.

en.L: "Please inquire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for us, for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will act with us according to all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders, and he will go up from [against] us."
en.B: "Please seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on our behalf, because Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon is at war with us. Perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do for us one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders, as in all the wonders of the past, so that the king will lift the siege and leave us."
en.R: "Please ask {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to help us. Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon is attacking us. Maybe {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do a miracle for us, like the ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did long ago. Then Nebuchadrezzar will stop attacking us and go away."

es.L: «Consulta, te ruego, {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} por nosotros, porque Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, nos hace la guerra. Quizás {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga con nosotros conforme a todas {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} maravillas, y él se retire de [sobre] nosotros».
es.B: «Por favor, consulta {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} por nosotros, porque Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, está en guerra contra nosotros. Quizás {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga por nosotros alguna de {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} maravillas, como todas las de antes, para que el rey levante el sitio y se vaya».
es.R: «Por favor, pídele {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} que nos ayude. Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, nos está atacando. Tal vez {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} haga un milagro por nosotros, como los que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo hace mucho tiempo. Así Nabucodorosor dejará de atacarnos y se irá».

fr.L: « Consulte donc {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour nous, car Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, nous fait la guerre. Peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} agira-t-il envers nous selon toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} merveilles, et il se retirera de [devant] nous. »
fr.B: « Consulte donc {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} pour nous, car Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, est en guerre contre nous. Peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera-t-il pour nous l’une de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} merveilles, comme toutes celles d’autrefois, et le roi lèvera le siège et nous laissera. »
fr.R: « S’il te plaît, demande {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} de nous aider. Nabuchodonosor, le roi de Babylone, nous attaque. Peut-être que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fera un miracle pour nous, comme ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a faits autrefois. Alors Nabuchodonosor arrêtera de nous attaquer et il s’en ira. »

sw.L: "Tafadhali utuulizie kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa maana Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli anafanya vita juu yetu. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatutendea sawasawa na maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yote, naye atapanda kutuacha."
sw.B: "Tafadhali umtafute {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa ajili yetu, kwa sababu Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli anapigana nasi. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatutendea moja ya maajabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kama maajabu yote ya zamani, ili mfalme huyo aondoe jeshi lake aliloweka kuuzunguka mji, atuache."
sw.R: "Tafadhali mwombe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atusaidie. Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli anatushambulia. Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatutendea muujiza, kama miujiza aliyoifanya zamani. Ndipo Nebukadreza ataacha kutushambulia na kuondoka."

vi.L: "Xin hãy cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho chúng tôi, vì Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đang giao chiến với chúng tôi. Có lẽ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ làm cho chúng tôi theo mọi việc lạ lùng của Ngài, và hắn sẽ rút lui khỏi chúng tôi."
vi.B: "Xin ông cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp chúng tôi, vì Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đang đánh chúng tôi. Có lẽ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ làm cho chúng tôi một việc lạ lùng như mọi việc lạ lùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm xưa kia, để vua ấy giải vây và rút đi."
vi.R: "Xin ông cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giúp chúng tôi. Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa vua Ba-by-lôn đang tấn công chúng tôi. Có lẽ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ làm một phép lạ cho chúng tôi như những phép lạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã làm thuở xưa. Khi ấy Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa sẽ thôi tấn công và bỏ đi."

ko.L: "부디 우리를 위하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈어 주십시오. 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살이 우리를 치고 있습니다. 혹시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그분의 모든 기적대로 우리에게 행하셔서, 그가 우리에게서 물러갈지도 모릅니다."
ko.B: "우리를 위하여 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈어 주십시오. 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살이 우리를 공격하고 있습니다. 혹시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 옛날에 하신 그 모든 놀라운 일처럼 우리에게도 기적을 베푸셔서, 그 왕이 포위를 풀고 물러갈지도 모릅니다."
ko.R: "부디 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 우리를 도와 달라고 여쭈어 주십시오. 바빌론 왕 느부갓레살이 우리를 공격하고 있습니다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 옛날에 하신 것처럼 우리를 위해 기적을 베푸실지도 모릅니다. 그러면 느부갓레살이 공격을 멈추고 물러갈 것입니다."

pt.L: "Consulte, por favor, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} por nós, pois Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, está guerreando contra nós. Talvez {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} aja conosco segundo todas as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} maravilhas, e ele se retire de [cima de] nós."
pt.B: "Por favor, consulte {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} por nós, porque Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, está em guerra contra nós. Talvez {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} faça por nós uma das {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} maravilhas, como todas as maravilhas do passado, e o rei levante o cerco e nos deixe."
pt.R: "Por favor, peça {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} que nos ajude. Nabucodorosor, rei da Babilônia, está nos atacando. Talvez {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} faça um milagre por nós, como os que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} fez há muito tempo. Então Nabucodorosor vai parar de nos atacar e vai embora."

decisions.choice: inquire of the LORD: ask a prophet to seek a word from God
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek, and with God as its object it often means asking his will through a prophet in a time of crisis (1 Kings 22:8; 2 Kings 22:13, 18). The king wants Jeremiah to pray and to bring back the LORD's answer.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the king of Babylon (605-562 BC), the same king as Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: This is the first time the book names him. Jeremiah usually spells the name with an r, Nebuchadrezzar, which is closer to the Babylonian form Nabu-kudurri-usur; chapters 27-29 and the books of Kings and Chronicles use Nebuchadnezzar. Each verse keeps the form its own text uses. It is one man either way.

decisions.choice: his wonders: the great saving acts of the LORD in Israel's past
decisions.reason: The word is used of the miracles of the exodus (Exodus 3:20; Psalm 78:11-12). The king may also be thinking of the night a century earlier when the LORD struck the Assyrian army and Sennacherib went home from Jerusalem (Isaiah 37:36-37; 2 Kings 19:35-36). He hopes for the same rescue. The answer in verse 5 turns the language of the exodus against the city.

decisions.choice: go up from us: withdraw, lift the siege
alternatives: the LORD will go up from us
decisions.reason: An army that "goes up from" a city it is attacking marches away. The same words are used in 37:5, 11 when the Babylonians broke off the siege for a time. The subject is the king of Babylon.

decisions.choice: so that the king will lift the siege and leave us (B); a miracle ... like the ones he did long ago ... Then Nebuchadrezzar will stop attacking us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king as the one who withdraws, and Readable says "miracle" for the wonders and makes clear that they belong to the past.

decisions.choice: Nabucodorosor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here has the form with -r- (Nebuchadrezzar), so every level writes "Nabucodorosor", as the terms note sets; it is the same king as Nabucodonosor (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Nebukadreza
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew mostly spells the king's name with r, so Swahili keeps that form here, as the English does; Kings and Chronicles have "Nebukadneza", and he is the same king.

decisions.choice: "Nabuchodonosor" for both Hebrew spellings, Nebuchadrezzar and Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for the whole book: French readers know this king only as "Nabuchodonosor", and the meaning decision explains that the two Hebrew spellings name one king, so French does not mark the difference.

decisions.choice: "Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa" (Nebuchadrezzar)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's usual Hebrew form of the name has r, and the terms note keeps it as "Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa" wherever the Hebrew has it; the published "Nê-bu-cát-nết-sa" of 2 Kings is used wherever the Hebrew has the form with n, as it mostly does in chapters 27-29. It is the same king.

decisions.choice: "느부갓레살"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's Hebrew here has the form Nebuchadrezzar; as the terms note, each verse keeps its own form (느부갓레살 here, 느부갓네살 where the Hebrew has it), and meaning decision m2 says they are the same king.

decisions.choice: The king's envoys speak to Jeremiah in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Officials asking a prophet to inquire of God speak politely, as in 2 Kings 19.

decisions.choice: Nabucodorosor
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Jeremiah usually spells the king's name with an r (m2), and the English keeps "Nebuchadrezzar" there; Portuguese keeps the difference with "Nabucodorosor", and writes "Nabucodonosor", the form of 2 Kings 24-25, wherever the Hebrew and the English have the n.

decisions.choice: você (the king's messengers to Jeremiah)
decisions.reason: As 1:5 sets it for the book (r-pt-1 there): the king and his officials speak to Jeremiah with "você", as people speak to each other in this translation; "o senhor" is kept for a king or a master, and "tu" for God.

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְרֻ֖ן אֶל־צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃

en.L: And Jeremiah said to them, "Thus you shall say to Zedekiah:

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel: Look I [am] turning back the weapons of the war which [are] in your hand, which you [are] fighting with them [against] the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans, the [ones] besieging you from outside to the wall; and I will gather them into [the] middle of the city this.

en.L: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Look, I am turning back the weapons of war that are in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the wall; and I will gather them into the middle of this city.
en.B: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: I am about to turn back the weapons of war in your hands, the weapons you are using to fight the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you from outside the wall. I will gather them into the heart of this city.
en.R: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: You are using your weapons to fight the king of Babylon and the Babylonians, who are surrounding you outside the city wall. But I will turn those weapons back. I will pile them up in the center of this city, where they are of no use.

es.L: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: He aquí, yo hago volver atrás las armas de guerra que [están] en {{plural_you:sus manos|vuestras manos}}, con las que {{plural_you:ustedes pelean|vosotros peleáis}} contra el rey de Babilonia y contra los caldeos que {{plural_you:los|os}} sitian fuera del muro; y las reuniré en medio de esta ciudad.
es.B: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Voy a hacer retroceder las armas de guerra que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} en las manos, las armas con que {{plural_you:pelean|peleáis}} contra el rey de Babilonia y contra los caldeos que {{plural_you:los|os}} sitian desde fuera del muro. Las reuniré en el centro de esta ciudad.
es.R: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: {{plural_you:Ustedes están|Vosotros estáis}} usando {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} armas para pelear contra el rey de Babilonia y contra los babilonios, que {{plural_you:los|os}} tienen rodeados fuera del muro de la ciudad. Pero yo haré retroceder esas armas. Las amontonaré en el centro de esta ciudad, donde no {{plural_you:les|os}} servirán de nada.

fr.L: “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : Voici, je retourne les armes de guerre qui sont dans vos mains, avec lesquelles vous combattez le roi de Babylone et les Chaldéens qui vous assiègent hors de la muraille ; et je les rassemblerai au milieu de cette ville.
fr.B: “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël, dit ceci : Je vais retourner les armes de guerre qui sont dans vos mains, celles avec lesquelles vous combattez le roi de Babylone et les Chaldéens qui vous assiègent hors de la muraille. Je les rassemblerai au cœur de cette ville.
fr.R: “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu d’Israël : Vous vous servez de vos armes pour combattre le roi de Babylone et les Babyloniens qui vous encerclent, hors de la muraille de la ville. Mais je vais retourner ces armes contre vous. Je les entasserai au centre de cette ville, où elles ne serviront à rien.

sw.L: '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Tazama, ninazigeuza silaha za vita zilizo mikononi mwenu, ambazo mnapigana nazo na mfalme wa Babeli na Wakaldayo wanaowazingira nje ya ukuta; nami nitazikusanya katikati ya mji huu.
sw.B: 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Ninakaribia kuzirudisha nyuma silaha za vita zilizo mikononi mwenu, silaha mnazotumia kupigana na mfalme wa Babeli na Wakaldayo wanaowazingira kutoka nje ya ukuta. Nitazikusanya katikati ya mji huu.
sw.R: 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Mnatumia silaha zenu kupigana na mfalme wa Babeli na Wababeli, ambao wameuzunguka mji nje ya ukuta. Lakini nitazirudisha nyuma silaha hizo. Nitazirundika katikati ya mji huu, mahali ambapo hazitawafaa kitu.

vi.L: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán thế này: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho các khí giới chiến tranh trong tay các ngươi quay ngược lại, là những khí giới các ngươi đang dùng để chiến đấu với vua Ba-by-lôn và người Canh-đê đang vây hãm các ngươi bên ngoài tường thành; và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ gom chúng vào giữa thành này.
vi.B: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán như vầy: Ta sắp làm cho các khí giới trong tay các ngươi quay ngược lại, là những khí giới các ngươi đang dùng để đánh vua Ba-by-lôn và người Canh-đê đang vây hãm các ngươi bên ngoài tường thành. Ta sẽ gom chúng vào giữa thành này.
vi.R: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, phán: Các ngươi đang dùng vũ khí để đánh vua Ba-by-lôn và quân Ba-by-lôn đang vây quanh bên ngoài tường thành. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho các vũ khí ấy quay ngược lại. Ta sẽ chất đống chúng giữa thành này, nơi chúng chẳng còn dùng được.

ko.L: '이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 보아라, 너희가 바빌론 왕과, 성벽 밖에서 너희를 포위하고 있는 갈대아 사람들과 싸우려고 너희 손에 든 전쟁 무기들을 내가 되돌리고, 그것들을 이 성 한가운데로 모으겠다.
ko.B: '이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 너희가 성벽 밖에서 너희를 포위하고 있는 바빌론 왕과 갈대아 사람들과 싸우려고 손에 들고 있는 무기들을 내가 되돌리겠다. 내가 그것들을 이 성 한가운데로 모으겠다.
ko.R: '이스라엘의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 너희는 무기를 들고 바빌론 왕과 바빌로니아 사람들과 싸우고 있다. 그들은 성벽 밖에서 너희를 에워싸고 있다. 그러나 내가 그 무기들을 되돌리겠다. 내가 그것들을 이 성 한가운데에 쌓아 두겠다. 거기에서는 아무 쓸모가 없을 것이다.

pt.L: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: Eis que eu faço voltar as armas de guerra que [estão] nas mãos de vocês, com as quais vocês estão lutando contra o rei da Babilônia e os caldeus que sitiam vocês de fora do muro; e eu as ajuntarei no meio desta cidade.
pt.B: 'Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel: Estou para fazer recuar as armas de guerra que vocês têm nas mãos, as armas que vocês estão usando para lutar contra o rei da Babilônia e contra os caldeus que cercam vocês do lado de fora do muro. Eu as recolherei no coração desta cidade.
pt.R: 'É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, o Deus de Israel, diz: Vocês estão usando as suas armas para lutar contra o rei da Babilônia e contra os babilônios, que estão cercando vocês do lado de fora do muro da cidade. Mas eu vou fazer essas armas recuarem. Vou amontoá-las no centro desta cidade, onde não vão servir para nada.

decisions.choice: turning back the weapons of war: making Judah's defense fail and retreat
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn something around or make it go back. The LORD will make the defenders' weapons useless: their fighting will be pushed back from the walls into the city. It may also suggest the weapons being turned against those who hold them.

decisions.choice: gather them: the weapons, driven back from outside the wall into the city
alternatives: the Chaldeans, whom the LORD will bring into the city
decisions.reason: "Them" most naturally points back to the weapons, the nearest plural that the verse is about: the battle will be lost outside and the arms heaped up inside, where they cannot help. Others take "them" as the Chaldeans: the LORD will bring the enemy right into the middle of the city. Both readings end with the city taken.

decisions.choice: from outside the wall: where the Chaldeans are besieging the city
decisions.reason: The phrase stands next to "who are besieging you" and describes the enemy camp around the walls.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were a people of southern Mesopotamia whose dynasty, Nebuchadrezzar's, ruled Babylon at this time. In Jeremiah the name means the Babylonian army and nation.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah, Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans".

decisions.choice: I will pile them up in the center of this city, where they are of no use
decisions.reason: Readable puts the sentence in a clearer order and says why the weapons are gathered in.

decisions.choice: los caldeos (Literal, Balanced); los babilonios (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans keep the published wording of 2 Kings 25:4-5 throughout the block.

decisions.choice: Wakaldayo (Literal, Balanced); Wababeli (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili for the Chaldeans (2 Chronicles 36:17); Readable names them by their country.

decisions.choice: "les Chaldéens" (L, B); "les Babyloniens" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note and 2 Kings 25 in French: Readable names them by the name readers know, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "người Canh-đê" (L, B); "quân Ba-by-lôn" or "người Ba-by-lôn" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for the Chaldeans, as 2 Kings 25; Readable names them as the Babylonians, as the English Readable does, used so through these chapters.

decisions.choice: "갈대아 사람들" (L, B); "바빌로니아 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms for the Chaldeans, as 2 Kings 25:4; Readable names the people as the English Readable does, and "바빌론" stays the city and the king's title.

decisions.choice: os caldeus (L, B); os babilônios (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, where the name first appears (m4): "os caldeus" at Literal and Balanced, the Portuguese name of the people whose dynasty ruled Babylon, and "os babilônios" at Readable, as the English Readable says "Babylonians", as Isaiah does.

records.literal_gloss: And will fight I with you with hand outstretched and with arm strong, and in anger and in fury and in wrath great.

en.L: And I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will fight against you with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm, and in anger and in fury and in great wrath.
en.B: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will fight against you with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand stretched out and with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} strong arm, in anger, in fury and in great rage.
en.R: I {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} will fight against you with all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power. I will stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand and use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} strong arm against you, because I am angry, furious and full of rage.

es.L: Y yo mismo pelearé contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con mano extendida y con brazo fuerte, y con ira, y con furor, y con gran enojo.
es.B: Yo mismo pelearé contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano extendida y con {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo fuerte, con ira, con furor y con gran enojo.
es.R: Yo mismo pelearé contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} con todo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} poder. Extenderé {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano y usaré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} brazo fuerte contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, porque estoy enojado, furioso y lleno de indignación.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je combattrai contre vous avec une main étendue et avec un bras fort, avec colère, avec fureur et avec un grand courroux.
fr.B: Moi-même, je combattrai contre vous, la main tendue, avec la force de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} bras, avec colère, avec fureur, avec une grande indignation.
fr.R: Moi-même, je vais combattre contre vous avec toute {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} puissance. Je tendrai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main et je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servirai de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} bras puissant contre vous, parce que je suis en colère, furieux et plein d’indignation.

sw.L: Nami {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitapigana nanyi kwa mkono ulionyoshwa na kwa mkono wenye nguvu, na kwa hasira, na kwa ghadhabu, na kwa ukali mkuu.
sw.B: Mimi {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitapigana nanyi kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ulionyoshwa na kwa mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wenye nguvu, kwa hasira, kwa ghadhabu na kwa ukali mkuu.
sw.R: Mimi {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} nitapigana nanyi kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} zote. Nitaunyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} na kutumia mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wenye nguvu dhidi yenu, kwa sababu nimekasirika, nimeghadhibika na nimejaa ukali.

vi.L: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chiến đấu nghịch cùng các ngươi bằng bàn tay giơ ra và bằng cánh tay mạnh mẽ, trong cơn giận, trong cơn thịnh nộ và trong cơn phẫn nộ lớn.
vi.B: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chiến đấu nghịch cùng các ngươi bằng bàn tay giơ ra và cánh tay mạnh mẽ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, trong cơn giận, cơn thịnh nộ và cơn phẫn nộ lớn.
vi.R: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ dùng hết quyền năng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà chiến đấu nghịch cùng các ngươi. Ta sẽ giơ tay ra và dùng cánh tay mạnh mẽ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chống lại các ngươi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đang giận dữ, thịnh nộ và phẫn nộ vô cùng.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 친히 편 손과 강한 팔로, 진노와 분노와 큰 격노로 너희와 싸우겠다.
ko.B: 내가 친히 손을 뻗고 강한 팔을 휘둘러, 진노와 분노와 크게 타오르는 격노로 너희를 치겠다.
ko.R: 내가 직접 온 힘을 다해 너희와 싸우겠다. 내가 손을 뻗고 강한 팔을 휘둘러 너희를 치겠다. 나는 화가 나고, 몹시 노하고, 분노로 가득 차 있다.

pt.L: E eu mesmo lutarei contra vocês com mão estendida e com braço forte, e com ira, e com furor, e com grande indignação.
pt.B: Eu mesmo lutarei contra vocês com a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão estendida e com o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} braço forte, com ira, com furor e com grande indignação.
pt.R: Eu mesmo vou lutar contra vocês com todo o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} poder. Vou estender a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão e usar o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} braço forte contra vocês, porque estou irado, furioso e cheio de indignação.

decisions.choice: outstretched hand and strong arm: the power that rescued Israel from Egypt, now turned against Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Moses spoke of the LORD bringing Israel out of Egypt "with a strong hand and an outstretched arm" (Deuteronomy 26:8; also 4:34; 5:15). Here the two words trade places, and the power is aimed at God's own people. The king hoped for a wonder like those of the past (verse 2); he will get one, but against himself.

decisions.choice: I myself will fight against you
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is added to a verb that already carries it, for emphasis. It is not only Babylon that Judah faces, but the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: anger, fury, great wrath: three words for God's anger piled up
decisions.reason: The three words together express the full force of God's anger at long-continued sin. The same three are found together in Deuteronomy 29:27 and Jeremiah 32:37.

decisions.choice: with all my power. I will stretch out my hand and use my strong arm
decisions.reason: Readable says what the hand and arm stand for and keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: yo mismo
decisions.reason: God's "I" takes no deity_pronoun span in Spanish, so "yo mismo" is written plainly where the English spans "myself".

decisions.choice: "Moi-même" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The stressed pronoun stands at the start of the sentence, where French writes the capital plainly, as the style guide says for a pronoun beginning a sentence.

decisions.choice: "Chính Ta"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks the emphatic "I myself" with "chính"; "Ta" at the start of the sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: "진노와 분노와 큰 격노"
decisions.reason: Three Korean words for God's anger, as the Hebrew piles up three (meaning decision m3); Readable turns them into three short statements.

decisions.choice: eu mesmo (no span)
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts "myself" under the deity_pronoun setting. Portuguese says "eu mesmo", and "eu" for God takes no span (as Isaiah writes "Eu mesmo"), so the Literal of this verse, which has no "my", has no span.
